question: Does the escape-time constant (T x p, about 60 updates for cnn_l at entropy 0.05) change with model width and exploration while 1/p scaling holds?
setup: 7x7 room, vendored gw.py and ppo.py unchanged; cnn_xl (c=16, h=128) registered at run time. Same readout, escape and switch-back definitions as escape-time-v1 (gem reached on >= 50% of battery trials; 8 sampled rollouts per trial; measure3 7x7 = frozen v2).
stopping: 250-update segments; a run stops once every seed has escaped and stayed >= 0.5 for 4 more checkpoints, or at its cap (unescaped seeds right-censored at the last checkpoint).
order: p 0.2 cells first (all widths and entropies), then p 0.05; within p, cnn_s, cnn_l, cnn_xl, entropy 0.05 then 0.01.
model: censored normal (Tobit) regression of log T. Cell = width x entropy (6 cells). M0: one intercept + slope b on log(1/p). M1: 6 intercepts + common b. M2: 6 intercepts + 6 slopes. Common sigma.

primary.H1_scaling: in M1, the 95% profile CI for b lies inside [0.75, 1.25]: 1/p scaling holds across width and exploration.
primary.H2_exponent_homogeneous: likelihood-ratio test M2 vs M1 (5 df): p >= 0.05 supported (no evidence the exponent varies); p < 0.05: exponent varies by cell.
primary.H3_constant_moves: likelihood-ratio test M1 vs M0 (5 df): p < 0.05 supported (the constant depends on width and/or exploration).

secondary: directional: the constant falls with width (cnn_s > cnn_l > cnn_xl) and is lower at entropy 0.05 than 0.01, read from M1 intercepts with 95% intervals
replication: cnn_l entropy 0.05 cell constant vs escape-time-v1 (median p x T = 57)
per-cell p x T medians, censoring counts, switch-backs
limits_declared: 4 seeds per cell; two p values per cell; entropy 0.01 cells may be censored at the cap, handled by the censored model.
